facts.statement: The setup plugin registers --setup-show as an alias that sets the setupshow option and describes it as showing fixture setup during test execution.
After fixture setup, setup-show stores an explicit fixture ID when present; otherwise it stores request.param itself in fixturedef.cached_param before displaying the SETUP action.
Directly parametrized test arguments are converted into artificial FixtureDef objects whose final two constructor arguments are False.
FixtureDef defines its final constructor parameters as unittest followed by ids, so the artificial direct-parameter FixtureDef has ids=False.
When cached_param exists, setup display interpolates it with "[{}]".format(fixturedef.cached_param), which performs implicit string formatting rather than calling a representation helper.
The same cached parameter is displayed during teardown and is deleted afterward.
The repository provides saferepr, which returns a size-limited representation and is designed to handle exceptions raised while producing representations.
Existing setup-display parameter coverage exercises --setup-only, --setup-plan, and --setup-show through a shared mode fixture.
Existing setup-display tests cover string-valued fixture parameters and assert that their values appear in SETUP and TEARDOWN output.
Existing parametrization tests define Python 3 bytes ID behavior, including b"ascii" producing the ID string "ascii".

scope_summary: Base-commit inspection found the BytesWarning path in setup-display formatting and the existing safe-representation utility and tests relevant to parameter display.
